question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core-owned, checked localization coverage manifest and required CI gate now, or should this governance model remain an RFC until the maintainers define permanent ownership and release policy?
rationale: The patch creates a new cross-product package, a repository-wide required check, and a release-governance model; correctness of the mechanics does not determine whether that long-lived core boundary is the intended product direction.

options.title: Sponsor the governance contract
options.body: Accept the owner-declared manifest and required coverage check as the localization foundation, then request a rebased ordered series with exact-head proof.

options.title: Keep it at RFC stage
options.body: Defer the core package and required check until maintainers define the supported release claims, accountable owners, and rollout scope.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the governance contract
recommendation.body: Accept the owner-declared manifest and required coverage check as the localization foundation, then request a rebased ordered series with exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended boundaries and split/rebase sequence, while the actual product decision remains with the repository’s designated maintainers.
